meta: starter_level=S2; path=SC; skills=randint,boundary,elif-chain,concat-str; solo=false; dictates=1; foreign_names=mana; story_beat=protected; echo=static fallback
Starter: the task-group headers (A, B, C), the tiers as comments, `road_roll = 0` (a placeholder, so the starter runs) and the first two branches with `___` text blanks (teacher's ruling: part B was a blank editor; the pre-fill saves groups 1 and 3 a few minutes). The placeholder gets 'still holds the starter's `0`' and a `___` left gets 'still holds the starter's `___`'. The tier skeleton (Show me more) is the assemble lines plus the last hint. Checks: RND (scripted die, args (1, 20)) and BND over scripted rolls 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 11, 15, 16, 17, 19, 20: same-tier rolls give the same encounter, neighbouring tiers give different ones (whole numbers masked, so an encounter that shows the roll is still one text per tier: loosened after the check-breaker probe), and the printed line starts with `Rolled <road_roll>: <encounter>` for rolls 7 and 20 (extra words after it, like a period, are fine: loosened too). A second randint call gets another number, so a printed line that rolls again instead of gluing in `road_roll` fails. Any encounter text passes (lint e); 'Use Mar'tu's picks' is a note with five ready-made texts. Other right tables pass (probed): top-down (`== 20`, `>= 16`, `>= 7`, `>= 2`, else), `and` ranges, `< 7`, `<= 1`, `<= 20` with no else, and the comma print. Echo spot (2.11): the spec has Mar'tu react to one tier's text; the schema has no echo field yet, so the pass line is the privacy-safe static fallback ('Hm. Noted.'). Lucky's side quest (old group D): Dumb Luck rerolls a 1 once, and a perception check with `and not night_time`. No WA depends on the real die: the main run never crashes for one roll and not another.

CP3 reruns with `"Option 4"`, `"OPTION 3"` and `"oPTION 4"`, so typing the value in small letters, or an `or` for each capital, fails. CP1 and CP2 rerun with small letters, so they stay green while the quiet slip is open. STREXACT looks only at text in a comparison (the starter's capital value is fine). `.lower` with no `()` is caught in CP1 (it breaks every reply). The WA 'both loud slips mended' stands in for partial 2. explainer='lean'.
